messages:
Sam (PM): FYI incoming request from QuantaPay — they want a dedicated pool for chat + embeddings with predictable p95 latency <=250ms and the ability to handle short promotional bursts up to ~400 concurrent chats for ~30 minutes. They need sizing guidance, autoscale recommendations, and a rough cost delta for contract.

Elaine (Sales): Customer launch target June 15. They want 99.9% uptime SLA. Budget is tight but they can pay for reserved burst capacity if we can justify it.

Mike (Infra Eng): Quick note — need model choice. If they insist on 13B-class quality (quantized) we should assume ~1000 tok/s per A100-equivalent on our optimized runtime; smaller models will change numbers a lot. Can we confirm target model?

Sam (PM): They asked for "production-grade responses comparable to our standard redwood-13b profiles". Assume redwood-13b-q4 for initial sizing.

Mike (Infra Eng): Rough calc:
- steady concurrent sessions: 250
- avg response size: 200 tokens
- average reply rate per session: 0.5 rps (1 reply every 2s) -> tokens/sec = 250 * 200 * 0.5 = 25,000 tok/s
- at 1000 tok/s per GPU -> ~25 GPUs steady
- burst to 400 sessions -> 40 GPUs (rounded up)

Tara (SRE): That seems sensible. Important ops notes: warm pool matters. Spinning GPUs cold adds 2–3 minutes; warm instances (pre-loaded weights + warmed caches) reduce that to <15s. For 30-minute promos we should pre-warm a warm_pool sized for expected burst.

Mike (Infra Eng): Recommendation (draft):
```
autoscale:
  min_instances: 20   # steady-state buffer
  max_instances: 60   # headroom for aggressive bursts & background ops
  warm_pool: 20       # pre-warmed instances reserved for <1min scale-ups
  scale_window_sec: 120
  cooldown_sec: 60
  metric: concurrent_sessions
  step: 4
```
This keeps steady ~25 GPUs but reserves headroom and warm capacity.

Lee (Solutions Eng): Also push caching + batching: prefix/KV caching for the top 50 common prompts can shave 15–30% tokens. Recommend a separate smaller embedding pool (8 GPUs) to avoid contention — embeddings have very different perf characteristics.

Elaine (Sales): Customer is ok with separate pools. Asks: can we provide an estimated monthly cost delta (reserved vs pure on-demand) and SLA text for the contract? Need to send by EOD tomorrow.

Sam (PM): Action items:
- Mike: run a synthetic workload sim (steady + burst) and produce a cost estimate + capacity table by EOD tomorrow.
- Tara: write warm-pool runbook and failure modes (e.g., cold start mitigation, autoscale safety limits).
- Lee: produce caching/embedding separation doc and sample prompt whitelist.
Please ack and add anything I missed.

Mike (Infra Eng): ack — will run sims and include cost assumptions (cloud GPU list pricing + overheads).

Tara (SRE): ack — will draft runbook and include playbook steps for manual override.

Lee (Solutions Eng): ack — will share prompt set and expected token savings.

Sam (PM): Thanks all :thumbsup: Let's plan a 2pm sync tomorrow if any of the calcs need discussion.
